label: j-initial sequence, step 4-5, after t/s/w (often on z)
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.002% of steps). Almost all mass (97%) is on sequences whose first token is j. It fires late in the original phase, mostly at t=4-5 (with a little at t=3/6 and on <DEL> when L=4-5), and only after t/s/w have shown up earlier in the prefix, e.g. j y s t t [z], j 1 s w [z], j s s t [w][<DEL>]. The input z is the strongest trigger (60% of mass, and all the top activations). It also fires when the previous two inputs are t/s/w. It never fires in the copy phase or at t<3, and practically never without a leading j. Precision is low (~0.2): plenty of j-initial prefixes containing t/s/w at step 4-5 do not activate it, so the exact conjunction is fuzzy. Activations are larger when the input is z and when there are several t/w tokens.
